statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-2303 (GO-2026-5327, GHSA-cp6g-7hqx-qxhp) is a heap out-of-bounds read in the C wrapper behind the mongo-go-driver's GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication, fixed in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver v1.17.7 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cp6g-7hqx-qxhp, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5327, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/GODRIVER-3770); the advisory's vulnerable symbol is mongo.Connect. That wrapper (x/mongo/driver/auth/internal/gssapi/gss_wrapper.c) is compiled only with cgo and the gssapi build tag: gss.go there carries the constraint gssapi && (linux || darwin) and imports "C", and without the tag x/mongo/driver/auth/gssapi_not_enabled.go builds instead (https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-go-driver/tree/v1.17.6/x/mongo/driver/auth). Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, on both x86_64 and aarch64: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 through 0.35.0-r2, each downloaded and checked against the index checksum. Each package holds two regular files, usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool, both statically linked Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0; the two architectures agree in every build. None was built with the gssapi tag. go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver v1.17.6 is in the Go build information of 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r6 only; builds from 0.32.1-r0 onward do not include the module at all. In 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r6, the Go function-name table (pclntab entries and inlined names) of both binaries, on both architectures, contains mongo-driver functions only from the BSON packages (bson, bson/bsoncodec, bson/bsonoptions, bson/bsonrw, bson/bsontype, bson/primitive and x/bsonx/bsoncore), which is the scan's in-binary positive control; no function or source file from the mongo client package, x/mongo/driver or its auth packages is present, so mongo.Connect and the GSSAPI code are not in any published build.

GO-2026-5327 (CVE-2026-2303, GHSA-cp6g-7hqx-qxhp): a heap out-of-bounds read in the error handling of mongo-go-driver's GSSAPI (Kerberos) authentication, fixed in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver 1.17.7; the advisory's affected symbol is mongo.Connect (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5327, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cp6g-7hqx-qxhp, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/GODRIVER-3770). The GSSAPI code is a C wrapper that the driver compiles only with cgo and its gssapi build tag; without them it compiles a stub that returns an error. Checked /usr/bin/trivy, the only file in every published trivy-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published (0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12, 38 builds each on x86_64 and aarch64), each verified against the repository index checksum, reading its Go build information (go version -m) and its Go symbol table (go tool nm). Each is a statically linked Go program for Linux, built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the Go FIPS 140-3 module (GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c). The builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.69.3-r5 carry go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver 1.17.6 but link only its BSON packages (bson, bson/bsoncodec, bson/bsonrw, bson/bsontype, bson/primitive and x/bsonx/bsoncore): no function of the go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo package, including mongo.Connect, and none of the driver's connection or authentication code under x/mongo/driver is in the symbol table. The builds from 0.69.3-r6 on do not contain mongo-driver. A search of the raw bytes of /usr/bin/trivy in 0.69.1-r0 and 0.74.0-r12, on both architectures, finds no go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo or x/mongo/driver name, while it finds runtime.main and, in 0.69.1-r0, the BSON packages. As a control, the same searches on a program built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against mongo-driver 1.17.6 that calls mongo.Connect find mongo.Connect.
